content:
In recent years, Macs have become increasingly affordable. With lower entry-level prices, more memory and storage capacity per dollar, and the launch of the MacBook Neo, Apple has for the first time become one of the most competitive value-for-money choices on the market.

Unfortunately, Apple has hiked prices significantly due to the ongoing memory shortage. Macs are no longer as attractive as they were a few weeks ago, but that said, there are still some decent deals out there—if you need a new computer, I would still say that when looking at the computer market as a whole, the Mac remains a worthwhile buy.

MacBook Air

Before the launch of the MacBook Neo, the MacBook Air was the entry-level option in Apple's laptop lineup. Although the arrival of the MacBook Neo has somewhat called its value proposition into question, I still believe the MacBook Air is an outstanding laptop if you want a better user experience without needing any high-end specifications.

MagSafe charging, a P3 wide-colour-gamut display, Center Stage for the webcam, and longer battery life are just a few of the MacBook Air's highlights. It also comes in a 15-inch version, unlike the MacBook Neo, which is only available in 13 inches.

The entire MacBook Air lineup currently has the following discounts:

  • M5 MacBook Air: 512GB storage, 16GB memory—on Amazon for $1,199 ($100 off!)

  • M5 MacBook Air: 1TB storage, 24GB memory—on Amazon for $1,699 ($100 off!)

15-inch MacBook Air:

  • M5 MacBook Air: 512GB storage, 16GB memory—on Amazon for $1,446 ($54 off)
  • M5 MacBook Air: 1TB storage, 16GB memory—on Amazon for $1,729 ($70 off)
  • M5 MacBook Air: 1TB storage, 24GB memory—on Amazon for $1,924 ($75 off!)

MacBook Neo

This product needs little introduction—the MacBook Neo is Apple's first affordable MacBook, priced at just $699.

Compared with the MacBook Air mentioned above, there are some trade-offs, but for the price it's still excellent. Build quality, display sharpness, and the macOS experience are essentially uncompromised. Of course, you have to accept the slower A18 Pro chip (though honestly, performance is by no means poor), fewer ports, and only 8GB of memory, but at this price it's a very reasonable deal. It also comes in some fun colours such as Citrus Yellow, Coral Pink and Indigo.

The MacBook Neo doesn't have any notable retail discounts at the moment, but if you're a student you can get $100 off from Apple. Otherwise, you can buy it on Amazon:

  • MacBook Neo: 256GB storage, 8GB memory—on Amazon for $689 ($10 off)
  • MacBook Neo: 512GB storage, 8GB memory, Touch ID—on Amazon for $789 ($10 off)

MacBook Pro

The top-of-the-line model in the laptop range is the MacBook Pro. You get the best specs available, but there is one important caveat. Apple is reportedly going to redesign the high-end MacBook Pro later this year, with OLED, a touchscreen and a slimmer chassis.

However, that redesign will debut only on models equipped with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips—so if you're buying the base model with the M5 chip, there is absolutely no problem picking up a new MacBook now. The same applies if you don't mind the redesign at all, since the M5 Pro and M5 Max are still outstanding new chips.
